# Alert

A short, colored message that tells the user about the result of an action or the state of the page.

## Import

```tsx
import { Alert } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The message body. |
| `tone` | `"info" \| "success" \| "danger"` | no | `"info"` | The meaning of the message. Sets the color. |
| `title` | `string` | no |  | Short bold summary shown above the message. |

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { Alert, Stack } from "@ds";

export function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Alert>Your trial ends in 3 days.</Alert>
      <Alert tone="success" title="Saved">
        Your changes are live.
      </Alert>
      <Alert tone="danger" title="Sign in failed">
        The email or password is incorrect.
      </Alert>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Pick `tone` by meaning: `info` for neutral notes, `success` after something worked, `danger` for errors. A `danger` alert is announced to screen readers immediately.

## Do

- `alert/form-error` Use `tone="danger"` for form-level errors, above the fields.
- `alert/short` Keep the message to one or two sentences.
- `alert/title` Use `title` for a short summary when the message needs one.

## Don't

- `alert/no-custom-message` Don't color a `<div>` or `<p>` to make a message. Use `Alert`.
- `alert/not-field-error` Don't use `Alert` for a single field's validation. Pass `error` to `TextField`.
- `alert/one-per-event` Don't stack several alerts for one event. Show one.

# Button

Triggers an action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.

## Import

```tsx
import { Button } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The button label. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary"` | no | `"secondary"` | Visual emphasis. Use at most one `primary` button per view. |
| `type` | `"button" \| "submit"` | no | `"button"` | Native button type. Use `submit` for the main action of a form. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Prevents interaction and dims the button. |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | no |  | Called when the button is activated. |

## Examples

### Variants

```tsx
import { Button, Stack } from "@ds";

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Stack direction="horizontal" gap="sm">
      <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
      <Button>Cancel</Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Use `variant="primary"` for the single most important action in a view and the default `secondary` variant for everything else.

## Do

- `button/one-primary` Use one `primary` button per view.
- `button/submit-type` Use `type="submit"` for the main action inside a `<form>`.
- `button/verb-labels` Write labels as verbs: "Sign in", "Save changes".

## Don't

- `button/no-raw-button` Don't style a raw `<button>` element. Use `Button`.
- `button/no-style-props` Don't pass `style` or `className`. `Button` does not accept them.
- `button/not-navigation` Don't use a `Button` for navigation. Use a link.

# Card

A bordered surface that groups related content, such as a form or a settings section.

## Import

```tsx
import { Card } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The card content. |
| `padding` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | no | `"lg"` | Inner padding, as a `space` token name. |

## Examples

### Settings section

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Heading, Stack, TextField } from "@ds";

export function SettingsSection() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <Stack gap="md">
        <Heading level={2}>Profile</Heading>
        <TextField label="Display name" name="displayName" />
        <Stack direction="horizontal" gap="sm">
          <Button variant="primary" type="submit">
            Save changes
          </Button>
        </Stack>
      </Stack>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Card` only draws the surface. Put a `Stack` inside it to space the content, and start it with a `Heading`.

## Do

- `card/one-topic` Use `Card` to group one topic: a form, a settings section, an empty state.
- `card/stack-inside` Put a `Stack` directly inside the card to space its content.
- `card/padding-token` Set `padding` with a `space` token name.

## Don't

- `card/no-div-card` Don't build a card from a `<div>` with a border and background. Use `Card`.
- `card/no-nesting` Don't nest a `Card` inside another `Card`.
- `card/no-invented-containers` Don't import `Container` or `Box` for grouping. They do not exist.

# Heading

A page or section title. Renders the matching `<h1>` to `<h3>` element.

## Import

```tsx
import { Heading } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The heading text. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3` | yes |  | The heading level. Renders `<h1>`, `<h2>` or `<h3>` and sets the size. |

## Examples

### Page title

```tsx
import { Heading, Stack } from "@ds";

export function PageTitle() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Heading level={1}>Settings</Heading>
      <Heading level={2}>Profile</Heading>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Choose `level` by document structure, not by size: one level 1 per page, level 2 for sections, level 3 inside sections.

## Do

- `heading/one-h1` Use exactly one `level={1}` heading per page.
- `heading/card-starts-h2` Start each `Card` with a `level={2}` heading.
- `heading/stack-spacing` Let `Stack` handle the space around headings.

## Don't

- `heading/no-raw-headings` Don't write raw `<h1>` to `<h6>` elements. Use `Heading`.
- `heading/no-font-size` Don't set a font size on a heading. `level` sets it.
- `heading/no-skipped-levels` Don't skip levels, such as a level 3 directly under a level 1.

# Stack

Lays out children in a row or column with consistent spacing between them. `Stack` is the only layout primitive in this design system.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stack } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The elements to lay out. |
| `direction` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | no | `"vertical"` | The axis children are placed along. |
| `gap` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | no | `"md"` | Space between children, as a `space` token name. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch"` | no | `"stretch"` | Alignment on the cross axis. |

## Examples

### Horizontal

```tsx
import { Button, Stack } from "@ds";

export function Horizontal() {
  return (
    <Stack direction="horizontal" gap="sm" align="center">
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
      <Button>Cancel</Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

### Vertical

```tsx
import { Stack, TextField } from "@ds";

export function Vertical() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="md">
      <TextField label="First name" name="firstName" />
      <TextField label="Last name" name="lastName" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Reach for `Stack` whenever elements need space between them. Nest stacks to combine rows and columns.

## Do

- `stack/all-spacing` Use `Stack` for all spacing between elements.
- `stack/nest-for-rows` Nest a horizontal `Stack` inside a vertical one for rows of actions.
- `stack/gap-token` Set `gap` with a `space` token name: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`.

## Don't

- `stack/no-invented-layout` Don't import `Box`, `Flex`, `Grid` or `Container`. They do not exist.
- `stack/no-flex-div` Don't write a `<div>` with `display: flex` or `gap`. Use `Stack`.
- `stack/no-px-gap` Don't pass pixel values to `gap`.

# TextField

A single-line text input with a built-in label and error message.

## Import

```tsx
import { TextField } from "@ds";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Visible label. Every field must have one. |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Field name submitted with the form. |
| `type` | `"text" \| "email" \| "password"` | no | `"text"` | Native input type. |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Controlled value. Omit for an uncontrolled field. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  | Called with the new value on every change. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no |  | Hint shown while the field is empty. Not a replacement for `label`. |
| `error` | `string` | no |  | Validation message. When set, the field is shown in an error state. |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Marks the field as required. |

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { TextField } from "@ds";

export function Basic() {
  return <TextField label="Email" name="email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />;
}
```

### With error

```tsx
import { TextField } from "@ds";

export function WithError() {
  return (
    <TextField
      label="Password"
      name="password"
      type="password"
      error="Enter at least 8 characters."
      required
    />
  );
}
```

## Usage

`TextField` renders its own `<label>` and wires it to the input, so pass `label` instead of writing a label element. Pass `error` to show a validation message.

## Do

- `textfield/label` Always pass `label`.
- `textfield/input-types` Use `type="email"` and `type="password"` for those fields.
- `textfield/stack-spacing` Put fields in a `Stack` to space them.

## Don't

- `textfield/no-raw-input` Don't use a raw `<input>` or `<label>`. Use `TextField`.
- `textfield/no-placeholder-label` Don't use `placeholder` as the label.
- `textfield/error-prop` Don't render your own error text under the field. Pass `error`.
